references.text: God's original command to Adam not to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, which 3:17 refers back to directly.
Paul explains how sin entered the world through one man (Adam) and how death spread to all people, in contrast to salvation through Christ.
Paul refers to the curse placed on creation after Adam's sin, and how all of creation groans and sighs while waiting for redemption.
Lamech names his son Noah and refers directly to the curse over the earth from Genesis 3:17, with hope for comfort from the toil of labor.
Land that bears thorns and thistles is worthless and near cursed—a picture that reflects the curse over the earth in Genesis 3:17-18.
The Preacher reflects on the vanity of human striving under the sun, which mirrors the curse of work from Genesis 3:17.
The contrast between the original freedom to eat from every tree and the subsequent curse that makes the earth a source of toil.
The theological contrast between the original gift of food without labor and the new condition where nourishment requires toil because of sin.
